meta.title: Two People, Same $10,000, Ten Years Apart. Here's The Gap Compounding Creates.
meta.hook: Two people each invest $10,000. Same return. The only difference is one started ten years earlier.
meta.description: A simple hypothetical: two investors each put in $10,000 once and never add another dollar, assuming a constant 8% average annual return for illustration. One starts at 25, the other at 35. By 65, the early starter's money is worth more than double the late starter's, purely from ten extra years of compounding. This is a hypothetical math example, not a projection or promise — actual investment returns vary and are never guaranteed. Educational content only, not financial advice.
